thread.title: Markets Unravel as Rising Treasury Yields Ignites Asset Reallocation into Bonds

author: MT Newswires
title: Markets Unravel as Rising Treasury Yields Ignites Asset Reallocation into Bonds
text:
Shutterstock photo Spooked by rising bond yields and the weakening dollar, global investors bailed out of equity assets overnight, sending bourses across Asia and Europe deep into negative territory. The sell-off accelerated overnight as the 10-year Treasury note pierced the 2.70% yield, sending the Nikkei 1.4% lower and permeating European bourses. Accordingly, Dow futures are indicating a 200+ point loss at the open.
Stocks were also weighed down by Monday's reports that Apple ( AAPL ) plans to slash iPhone X production, as well soft Japanese economic data in which the jobless rate unexpectedly rose to 2.8% and household spending fell by a much greater-than-expected 2.5%.
Ahead of the US open, the yield on the 10-year note was last at 2.709% and climbing, the dollar is lower against the major currencies, driving up the price of gold by more than $1 per ounce. Oil futures are lower with Brent crude holding under $70 per barrel.
On Tuesday's agenda is the Case Shiller house price index at 9 am ET, expected to show a 0.6% increase in November, and the January consumer confidence index, seen improving to 123.6 from 122.1 in December.
Also, the Federal Open Market Committee begins its two-day policy meeting today. Although the Fed is not expected to adjust monetary policy, Wall Street will be waiting to see if the tone of the policy statement shifts to a more hawkish bias.
In corporate news, shares of Harley-Davidson ( HOG ) are down by more than 5% in pre-market trade after reporting disappointing Q4 earnings, Pfizer ( PFE ) beat EPS and sales expectations, while McDonald ( MCD ) also beat Wall Street's forecasts. All three, however, are in the red in sympathy with the broader market sell-off.
In other news, the healthcare sector is coming under pressure following news that JP Morgan ( JPM ), Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.A, BRK.B) and Amazon (AMZN) are forming a joint company to improve healthcare for employees.
The three said they will pursue this objective through an independent company that is "free from profit-making incentives and constraints," with its initial focus on technology solutions to provide employees with simplified high-quality an transparent healthcare at a reasonable cost.
